# runpod_pod (Resource)

A Runpod pod, GPU or CPU, managed through the v2 REST API.

**If you are an AI agent:** set up through https://agents.runpod.io first, then follow
[Using the provider from an AI agent](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/runpod/runpod/latest/docs/guides/agent-setup) before you plan or apply.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "runpod_pod" "training" {
  name        = "training-pod"
  image       = "runpod/pytorch:2.8.0-py3.11-cuda12.8.1-cudnn-devel-ubuntu22.04"
  gpu_type_id = "NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090"
  gpu_count   = 1
  cloud       = "SECURE"
  disk        = 20

  # Start SSH and JupyterLab through the Runpod image conventions. SSH needs a
  # key registered on the account; both need their port exposed below.
  start_ssh     = true
  start_jupyter = true

  env = {
    MODEL_NAME = "llama-3"
  }

  ports = ["8888/http", "22/tcp"]
}

# A CPU pod: cpu_type_id replaces gpu_type_id, and vcpu_count comes from the
# flavor's catalog range (a power of two).
resource "runpod_pod" "preprocess" {
  name        = "preprocess-pod"
  image       = "runpod/pytorch:2.8.0-py3.11-cuda12.8.1-cudnn-devel-ubuntu22.04"
  cpu_type_id = "cpu5c"
  vcpu_count  = 4
  disk        = 20
}

# A pod built from a template instead of an image, with CUDA and host-size
# constraints on placement and a network volume for data that has to outlive
# the pod. persistent_volume { size, path } is the other mount kind; it
# replaces 1.x volume_in_gb / volume_mount_path, and network_volumes replaces
# network_volume_id.
resource "runpod_pod" "from_template" {
  name                   = "template-pod"
  template_id            = runpod_template.pod.id
  gpu_type_id            = "NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090"
  min_cuda_version       = "12.1"
  min_ram_per_gpu        = 8
  min_vcpu_count_per_gpu = 2
  data_center_ids        = [runpod_network_volume.data.data_center]

  network_volumes = [{
    volume_id = runpod_network_volume.data.id
    path      = "/runpod-volume"
  }]
}

resource "runpod_template" "pod" {
  name  = "template-pod-base"
  image = "runpod/pytorch:2.8.0-py3.11-cuda12.8.1-cudnn-devel-ubuntu22.04"
  disk  = 20
}

resource "runpod_network_volume" "data" {
  name        = "training-data"
  size        = 50
  data_center = "EU-RO-1"
}

# What the API reports back about a running pod.
output "training_cost_per_hour" {
  value = runpod_pod.training.cost
}

output "training_memory_in_gb" {
  value = runpod_pod.training.memory_in_gb
}

output "training_cuda_version" {
  value = runpod_pod.training.cuda_version
}

# The command the pod runs, as the exec-form lists the API decodes from args.
output "training_docker_entrypoint" {
  value = runpod_pod.training.docker_entrypoint
}

output "training_docker_start_cmd" {
  value = runpod_pod.training.docker_start_cmd
}
```

Complete, runnable configurations that use this resource live in the
[use-case modules](https://github.com/runpod/terraform-provider-runpod/tree/main/v2/modules);
the Guides section documents each one.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Pod display name.

### Optional

- `allowed_cuda_versions` (List of String) Acceptable CUDA versions on the host machine, as major.minor, e.g. ["12.8", "12.6"]. Matching is exact, so a version no machine reports yields a capacity error rather than a fallback. A non-empty list cannot be combined with min_cuda_version. GPU pods only, and the API neither returns nor updates it, so changing it replaces the pod.
- `args` (String) Arguments passed to the container entrypoint.
- `cloud` (String) Cloud tier: SECURE or COMMUNITY. Server default is SECURE. Changing it replaces the pod.
- `cpu_type_id` (String) CPU flavor identifier from the catalog, e.g. "cpu5c", for a CPU-only pod. Exactly one of gpu_type_id or cpu_type_id must be set, and a CPU pod also needs vcpu_count. Changing it replaces the pod.
- `data_center_ids` (List of String) Preferred data centers for placement. Create-time hint; the scheduler's pick lands in data_center_id. The API neither returns nor updates it, so changing it replaces the pod.
- `desired_state` (String) Managed lifecycle state: RUNNING or EXITED. When set, the provider starts/stops the pod to converge, and a refresh reports the pod's actual run state, so a pod stopped outside Terraform shows up as a plan diff and is started again on the next apply. Unset leaves the pod's run state unmanaged.
- `disk` (Number) Container disk in GB (ephemeral).
- `env` (Map of String) Environment variables. An update merges the configured keys into the pod's environment: a configured key is set, including a configured PUBLIC_KEY or JUPYTER_PASSWORD, and a key removed from the configuration is removed from the pod. Keys the configuration never held, such as a template's env and the PUBLIC_KEY / JUPYTER_PASSWORD that start_ssh / start_jupyter added, stay on the pod. The exception is the first apply that configures env after an import, or after env was left unset: state then holds the pod's whole environment, so every key the configuration leaves out is removed from the pod, template keys included, and only PUBLIC_KEY and JUPYTER_PASSWORD stay. The plan lists those removals.
- `global_networking` (Boolean) Enable global networking (private cross-datacenter IP). Requires an NVIDIA GPU and an eligible data center. Changes take effect on the next pod start/restart.
- `global_volumes` (Attributes List) Global volumes (runpod_global_volume) mounted into the pod. A global volume has no data center, so the pod can run in any data center. At most one, combinable with network_volumes and mutually exclusive with persistent_volume. Like network_volumes, the mount is fixed at create: adding it replaces the pod, the volume cannot change, and only the path can. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--global_volumes))
- `gpu_count` (Number) Number of GPUs. Server default is 1. Changing it replaces the pod.
- `gpu_type_id` (String) GPU type identifier from the catalog, e.g. "NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090". Exactly one of gpu_type_id or cpu_type_id must be set. Changing it replaces the pod.
- `image` (String) Docker image reference. Optional when template_id supplies one; at least one of image or template_id is required.
- `min_cuda_version` (String) Lowest acceptable CUDA version on the host machine, as major.minor, compared numerically: 12.11 is above 12.2. Use it for an open-ended floor and allowed_cuda_versions for an exact set; a non-empty set cannot be combined with it. GPU pods only, and the API neither returns nor updates it, so changing it replaces the pod.
- `min_ram_per_gpu` (Number) Minimum host system RAM in GB per requested GPU. A placement filter, not a resource request: the pod may be allocated more. GPU pods only, and the API neither returns nor updates it, so changing it replaces the pod.
- `min_vcpu_count_per_gpu` (Number) Minimum host vCPU count per requested GPU. A placement filter, not a resource request: the pod may be allocated more. GPU pods only, and the API neither returns nor updates it, so changing it replaces the pod.
- `network_volumes` (Attributes List) Network volumes mounted into the pod, replacing the 1.x network_volume_id attribute. The volume must live in the same data center as the pod. The API accepts one entry today; the list is the forward-compatible shape. Mutually exclusive with persistent_volume, and the API cannot remove a mount once the pod has it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--network_volumes))
- `persistent_volume` (Attributes) Host-local persistent storage, replacing the 1.x volume_in_gb and volume_mount_path attributes. Pinned to the pod's host machine, so the data does not survive a host failure; prefer network_volumes for anything you cannot recreate. Not available on CPU pods, and mutually exclusive with network_volumes. A template can supply one; the API cannot remove a mount once the pod has it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--persistent_volume))
- `ports` (List of String) Exposed ports, e.g. ["8888/http", "22/tcp"].
- `registry` (String) Registry credential ID (runpod_registry) for pulling private images. A template can supply one. Removing it from the configuration leaves the credential attached: the provider cannot clear it yet.
- `start_jupyter` (Boolean) Create-time flag telling the provisioner to start JupyterLab by injecting a generated JUPYTER_PASSWORD variable. Needs an image that honors the convention (the Runpod official images do) and "8888/http" in ports. The API never returns it and cannot change it, so changing it replaces the pod.
- `start_ssh` (Boolean) Create-time flag telling the provisioner to set up SSH access by injecting a PUBLIC_KEY variable carrying the account's registered SSH keys. Needs keys registered on the account, and an image that honors the convention (the Runpod official images do); the ssh.direct form also needs "22/tcp" in ports. The API never returns it and cannot change it, so changing it replaces the pod.
- `template_id` (String) Pod template to base the pod on, resolved at create time into the same container settings this resource sets directly (image, args, disk, ports, env, registry, persistent volume, SSH/Jupyter flags, CUDA versions); explicit attributes win, except env, which is merged per key with the pod's values winning. Must not be a serverless template. Changing it replaces the pod. The API does not link the created pod back to the template, so a pod created this way reports no template.
- `vcpu_count` (Number) Number of vCPUs for a CPU pod. Must be valid for the chosen cpu_type_id and a power of two. Changing it replaces the pod.

### Read-Only

- `cluster_id` (String) Cluster this pod belongs to, or null for a standalone pod. Cluster members are managed through the cluster, not this resource.
- `cluster_ip` (String) The pod's address on its cluster's private overlay network, or null until the address is assigned.
- `cost` (Number) Current cost in USD per hour. This replaces the 1.x cost_per_hr, which read the same number off the REST v1 pod. Zero while the pod is EXITED or TERMINATED.
- `created_at` (String) Creation timestamp in RFC 3339 format.
- `cuda_version` (String) CUDA version the host machine reports. Kept while the pod is stopped, since it resumes onto the same host. Null when unknown or not applicable, as on a CPU pod.
- `data_center_id` (String) Data center the scheduler placed the pod in.
- `docker_entrypoint` (List of String) Container entrypoint the pod runs, in exec form, e.g. ["/bin/bash", "-c"], as the API decodes it from args. Read-only. Set the command through args.
- `docker_start_cmd` (List of String) Container start command the pod runs, in exec form, as the API decodes it from args; when there is an entrypoint, this is the argument list passed to it. Read-only. Set the command through args.
- `id` (String) Pod identifier assigned by the API.
- `locked` (Boolean) Whether the pod is locked, which prevents stopping or resetting it.
- `machine_id` (String, Deprecated) Deprecated. Host machine the pod is placed on, read from the GraphQL API's pod. Null when that API does not report the pod, reports an empty machine id, or cannot be reached. Served by the deprecated GraphQL shim, because REST v2 does not report it yet. Removed once REST v2 reports it.
- `memory_in_gb` (Number) System RAM in GB allocated to the pod: across all requested GPUs on a GPU pod, or the flavor's allocation on a CPU pod.
- `runtime` (Attributes) Live utilization the API reports for a RUNNING pod; null in every other status. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--runtime))
- `started_at` (String) When the pod last started, in RFC 3339 format. Null until it has run.
- `status` (String) Pod lifecycle status as reported by the API, e.g. RUNNING, EXITED, PROVISIONING.
- `volume_encrypted` (Boolean, Deprecated) Deprecated. Whether the pod's volume is encrypted, read from the GraphQL API's pod: false for an unencrypted volume, null only when that API does not report the pod or cannot be reached. Served by the deprecated GraphQL shim, because REST v2 does not report it yet. Removed once REST v2 reports it.

Optional:

### Nested Schema for `network_volumes`

Required:

- `path` (String) Mount path inside the container, e.g. "/runpod-volume".
- `volume_id` (String) ID of an existing runpod_network_volume. Changing it replaces the pod.


<a id="nestedatt--persistent_volume"></a>
### Nested Schema for `persistent_volume`

Required:

- `path` (String) Mount path inside the container, e.g. "/workspace".
- `size` (Number) Persistent storage in GB, 10 or more.


<a id="nestedatt--runtime"></a>
### Nested Schema for `runtime`

Read-Only:

- `cpu_util` (Number) CPU utilization percentage, 0 to 100.
- `gpus` (Attributes List) One entry per attached GPU, in the order the API reports them. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--runtime--gpus))
- `memory_util` (Number) Memory utilization percentage, 0 to 100.
- `ports` (Attributes List) Port mappings the running pod was assigned. This is the runtime view of the configurable ports attribute: one entry per exposed port, with the address it is reachable on. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--runtime--ports))
- `uptime_seconds` (Number) Seconds since the container started.

<a id="nestedatt--runtime--gpus"></a>
### Nested Schema for `runtime.gpus`

Read-Only:

- `memory_util` (Number) GPU memory utilization percentage, 0 to 100.
- `util` (Number) GPU utilization percentage, 0 to 100.


<a id="nestedatt--runtime--ports"></a>
### Nested Schema for `runtime.ports`

Read-Only:

- `ip` (String) Address the port is reachable on.
- `private_port` (Number) Port inside the container.
- `public_port` (Number) Port published outside the container.
- `type` (String) Protocol of the mapping, e.g. http or tcp.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Pods are imported by pod id. The API does not return template_id, start_ssh,
# start_jupyter, allowed_cuda_versions, min_cuda_version, min_ram_per_gpu,
# min_vcpu_count_per_gpu or data_center_ids, so an import leaves them empty
# and each one the configuration sets forces replacement on the first apply.
# Name them in lifecycle { ignore_changes = [...] } before that apply. The
# import also reads the pod's whole env into state, so the first apply with a
# configured env removes every key the configuration leaves out, template keys
# included; PUBLIC_KEY and JUPYTER_PASSWORD stay on the pod. Copy the keys to
# keep into the configuration before that apply.
terraform import runpod_pod.training pod_abc123
```
